subject: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object

messages.author: fd98f08a6ab27905
messages.subject: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
parts:
Hi,

I need some advice:

I have build a reactiveValue object that contains a names list.

list <- reactiveValues()
list[["1"]] <- stuff
list[["2"]] <- more_stuff

I cannot completely wipe out one list section in this reactiveValue object, because the classical method

list["2"] <- NULL

produces an error, saying that single bracketing is not allowed for reactiveValue objects.

And

list[["2"]] <- NULL

of course deletes the content of the list section but not the section itself.

Any idea?

many thanks

messages.subject: Re: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
parts:
The reactiveValues object isn't a list, even though it has some list-like behavior... Can you explain why it's needed? 

One possible issue for deleting items is that the behavior for an item deleted from a reactiveValues object is not well-defined - what should happen if a reactive expression takes a dependency on values$x, but then values$x is removed?

-Winston

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
parts:
On Friday, October 4, 2013 5:48:07 AM UTC-5, Willi Fiebranz wrote:

And

list[["2"]] <- NULL

of course deletes the content of the list section but not the section itself.

I do that in some places, and so far it doesn't cause a problem because once you do that, list["2"]] will return NULL until you assign something else to that slot. So will list[["2"]]$foo$xyz. Therefore, if my observer sees a NULL it assumes the value was not initialized and proceeds accordingly. If there is a practical difference between an uninitialized value and a NULL value, you could just use some other placeholder for an uninitialized value such as "".

PS: You'll live a much happier life if you avoid using names that are numerals such as "2" and names that are also the names of base R functions such as "list". It's syntactically valid, but guaranteed to confuse the hell out of you sooner or later.

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
parts:
I'm assuming there is still no way to remove an element from a reactiveValues() ?
I also just ran into this issue. An annoying workaround is indeed to set an element to NULL and then always having to check if it's NULL, but it'd be much more convenient to be able to remove values from reactiveValues.

To answer Winston's question of "what would the behaviour be?": I think it can be as simple as possible - if a value is removed, just ignore it. Just like you can take dependency on inputs that don't actually exist, it will simply never fire if it doesn't exist, I don't see a problem with that personally.
